criterion: M3 exit criterion 2 (TAA ghosting and RMSE against the supersampled reference) and dated addition 8 (GTAO and SSR each against a CPU reference)
written: 2026-10-10, before the implementation and the first run
lessons_applied: From the shadow checks: every comparison carries a coverage bound so it cannot pass over nothing, every metric has a control that must fail it, and scene cameras are fixed here, before any result.
scenes: At 256 x 256 with the perspective-correct G-buffer: the built-in test scene from its own camera and from the near camera of evidence/m3-shadows-bounds.json method note 5 (eye 1.8, 3.2, 2.4 toward 0.8, 0.2, 1.0), Suzanne, and the helmet role's model (evidence/m3-scene-models.json). TAA uses the built-in test scene at 128 x 128.

gtao.model: Ground-truth-based ambient occlusion (Jimenez, Wu, Pesce, Jarabo 2016), cosine-weighted visibility from the horizon angles on 16 fixed slice directions, 16 steps a side, world radius 0.5, projected-normal integration (their eq. 10), no falloff, no bent normal, no multi-bounce term, no denoiser. Input: the view-space depth and normal of the G-buffer.
gtao.reference: Ray casts on raw/renderer/bvh.hpp: 1,024 stratified cosine-weighted directions a pixel from the surface point (offset 1e-3 along the normal); a direction is occluded when it hits within 0.5. Visibility is the unoccluded fraction.

vs_reference.what: GTAO against the ray-cast visibility on G-buffer pixels at least 8 pixels from the border
vs_reference.bound: mean |difference| <= 0.05 and 95th percentile <= 0.15 per scene (GTAO is screen-space; this records how good it is)

coverage.bound: at least 2,000 pixels per scene with reference visibility below 0.9

gpu_parity.what: the WGSL pass against the CPU GTAO on the same G-buffer
gpu_parity.bound: |gpu - cpu| <= 1e-3 on all but 0.1% of pixels

controls.what: (a) visibility 1 everywhere against the reference; (b) the GPU pass on a depth buffer with the scene's last mesh moved 1% of the scene extent
controls.bound: (a) fails the vs_reference bound, (b) fails gpu_parity

ssr.model: Screen-space mirror reflections: for each G-buffer pixel, the reflected view ray marched in screen space over the view depth (up to 20 units, 64 linear steps, then 8 bisection steps), with a thickness of 0.2 units; the result is a hit pixel or a miss.
ssr.reference: A BVH ray from the surface point (offset 1e-3 along the normal) along the mirror direction; its first hit H. A pixel is resolvable when H exists, projects inside the screen, and the G-buffer's surface at that pixel lies within two pixel footprints of H (H is visible).

hits.what: resolvable pixels whose SSR hit position (the G-buffer position at the hit pixel) lies within two pixel footprints of H; a footprint is 2 d tan(fovy / 2) / height at H's view depth d
hits.bound: at least 90% of resolvable pixels per scene

false_hits.what: pixels that are not resolvable where SSR reports a hit
false_hits.bound: at most 10% of those pixels per scene

coverage.bound: at least 2,000 resolvable pixels per scene

gpu_parity.what: the WGSL pass against the CPU SSR on the same G-buffer
gpu_parity.bound: the same hit pixel, or both a miss, on all but 0.1% of pixels

controls.what: (a) SSR with unlimited thickness against the false_hits bound; (b) the GPU pass on a depth buffer with the scene's last mesh moved 1% of the scene extent

taa.model: Temporal anti-aliasing written for this engine: Halton(2, 3) sub-pixel jitter over 16 phases, history reprojected by per-pixel motion (camera and object motion from the scene), sampled bilinearly, clipped to the YCoCg colour box of the current 3 x 3 neighbourhood (mean plus or minus 1.25 standard deviations), blended with weight 0.1 for the current frame; a disoccluded or off-screen history sample takes the current frame. Shading is Lambert from the sun plus 0.2 ambient on linear albedo, background 0.05; no tone map.
taa.reference: Each frame supersampled on the CPU rasterizer at 16 x 16 stratified samples per pixel, box filter.

sequences.pan: 64 frames; the camera pans along its right vector by 0.3 pixels a frame; the scene is static.
sequences.moving_box: 32 frames; the camera is fixed; the box moves along +x by 1.5 pixels a frame (in screen space at its centre).

rmse.what: pan sequence, frames 32 to 63: mean RMSE of the TAA frame against its supersampled reference, and of the unjittered single-sample frame against the same reference
rmse.bound: TAA RMSE <= 0.5 x the single-sample RMSE

ghosting.what: moving_box sequence, frames 16 to 31: the trail is the pixels the box covers in none of the reference at frame f but in some reference frame from f - 8 to f - 1; ghosting G = mean |TAA - reference| over the trail

coverage.bound: at least 500 trail pixels summed over frames 16 to 31

gpu_parity.what: the WGSL resolve fed the CPU's frames, motion and its own history, frame by frame, against the CPU resolve
gpu_parity.bound: |gpu - cpu| <= 1e-3 per channel on all but 0.1% of pixels in every frame

controls.what: (a) TAA without jitter against the rmse bound; (b) TAA without the colour clip against the ghosting bound; (c) the GPU resolve with its history shifted one pixel
controls.bound: (a) fails rmse, (b) fails ghosting, (c) fails gpu_parity

does_not_prove: Frame times; rough (glossy) reflections; AO or reflections of off-screen or hidden geometry, which screen-space methods cannot see; TAA under fast motion, thin geometry, transparency or animated textures; that the stand-in scenes cover a Sponza-class level.

method_note_1_2026_10_10.issue: The TAA model rejects disoccluded history by depth. That test alone removes most of the moving box's trail, so control (b), TAA without the colour clip, could pass the ghosting bound and fail to discriminate.
method_note_1_2026_10_10.change: Control (b) removes both the colour clip and the depth disocclusion test, which leaves plain history blending; it must fail ghosting. TAA with the clip but without the depth test, and with the depth test but without the clip, are run and reported as well, not gated.
method_note_1_2026_10_10.disocclusion: The depth test, stated now: the history is rejected when the previous frame's view depth at the reprojected position (nearest pixel) differs from the reprojected point's expected previous view depth by more than 2% of that depth plus 0.02 units.

method_note_2_2026_10_10.written: 2026-10-10, after the first CPU run of GTAO and SSR and before any change is run
method_note_2_2026_10_10.first_run: Failed. GTAO: mean |difference| 0.008 to 0.021 and p95 0.025 to 0.075 (inside the bounds), but three of four scenes miss the coverage bound (1,982, 807 and 1,338 occluded pixels against 2,000), and on those three the control (visibility 1 everywhere) also meets the bounds, so there the check cannot discriminate. On Suzanne GTAO (0.019) is further from the reference than the control (0.0075). An open plane alone reads up to 0.086 away from 1. SSR: 69% to 87% of resolvable pixels correct against the 90% bound, almost all of the rest misses; the near scene and Suzanne also fail or nearly fail coverage; false hits 0% to 0.5% pass, but the unlimited-thickness control reaches only 0.01% to 5.3%, so it does not discriminate.
method_note_2_2026_10_10.diagnosis: GTAO reconstructs each horizon sample at its pixel centre, which lies off the slice plane, so an open plane reads as partly occluded; the sample should sit at the exact slice position with the depth read from its pixel. SSR spends most of its 64 steps outside the screen: the 20-unit ray is not clipped to the view, so steps on screen are several pixels apart and skip the 0.2-unit thickness band.
changes: GTAO: a horizon sample's view position is rebuilt from its exact screen position and the depth of the pixel it falls in.
SSR: the march is clipped to the screen rectangle and the near plane before stepping; a step that lands behind the depth buffer starts the bisection, and the thickness applies to the refined point.
A fifth scene, fixed now: the interior role's model (evidence/m3-scene-models.json, ABeautifulGame today) under the same camera as Suzanne, for AO and reflection content.
Gating: a scene that misses a coverage bound is reported, not gated, for that metric; the metric must pass on every scene that meets coverage, and on at least two scenes.
A new SSR control (c), added before its first run: SSR with the normal replaced by the view vector must fail the hits bound. The unlimited-thickness control (a) stays reported.
